title: Minimum Cost Path with Teleportations
summary: Given a m x n grid and an integer k, find the minimum total cost to reach the bottom-right cell (m - 1, n - 1) from the top-left cell (0, 0).
statement: Given a m x n grid and an integer k, find the minimum total cost to reach the bottom-right cell (m - 1, n - 1) from the top-left cell (0, 0). You can make normal moves to the right or down, which cost the value of the destination cell, or use up to k teleports to any cell where the destination cell's value is less than or equal to the current cell's value, with no cost for teleports.
constraints: Both grid dimensions are between two and 80.
Right/down moves cost the destination value.
Up to k teleports may go free to any cell of value no greater than the source value.
hints: For one more teleport, a destination of value v can inherit the best prior cost at any source value at least v.
Sweep cell-value groups downward while maintaining the best previous-layer cost, then relax normal right/down moves.
Build the zero-teleport DP, repeat the value sweep and grid DP k times, and keep the best final cost.
The descending sweep exactly implements every legal free teleport; the row-major relaxation then covers every normal path following that teleport.
editorial: The descending sweep exactly implements every legal free teleport; the row-major relaxation then covers every normal path following that teleport.

tests.explanation: Move to value two, then five for cost seven and teleport to the final value five.
No useful non-increasing teleport improves the normal path cost nine.
